candidates.title: Native nitro inventory
candidates.current_design: Truck.nitro_stock_bcd is a packed decimal byte; motion manually borrows, shop increments decimal and shares stock_mut with upgrade bytes, HUD/results consume packed stock.
candidates.proposed_model: Truck owns a native NitroStock count with consume/refill operations. Shop uses item-specific stock operations instead of treating nitro and upgrades as the same mutable byte. Encode packed digits only at HUD, source asset caps and legacy snapshot/debug boundaries.
candidates.removed_machinery: Packed inventory storage, nibble borrow in movement, packed-decimal inventory increments in shop.
candidates.remaining_boundaries: Decode source shop caps; encode HUD digits and compatible semantic debug/legacy snapshot fields.
candidates.benefit: One inventory rule across purchasing, inactive conversion and driving; changing inventory presentation no longer affects movement.
candidates.difficulty_reason: Crosses shop, movement and serialization; byte-edge compatibility needs explicit characterization.
candidates.impact_reason: Replaces one shared representation across the complete inventory lifecycle.
candidates.risk: medium: press-edge/history and capped inactive-conversion order must remain exact.
candidates.owners_order: Truck owns stock. Shop checks affordability then cap before increment/debit; inactive conversion decrements wallet before cap; motion retains prepared guard/history before consumption and effects.
preserve: same speed, sprite and sound order
cap comparisons and extra wallet debit before capped early exit
coverage_gaps: Fresh source/reference-backed natural purchase→consume integration and HUD review required.
Establish all accepted noncanonical stock/cap byte behavior before choosing a compatibility conversion; never silently normalize old snapshots.
candidates.overlaps: R1 touches scheduler shop call site only; no dependency. M2 shares snapshot/HUD files but separate state.
candidates.bounded_scope: Nitro only, keeping wallet arithmetic, upgrades, button histories and movement physics intact.

candidates.title: Native race elapsed units
candidates.current_design: RaceTimer stores three packed decimal bytes. advance_timer propagates decimal carry and immediately returns tile codes; results compare/store the upper two bytes.
candidates.proposed_model: Store elapsed source timing units as a native integer, advance by sixteen per service and freeze at the same threshold crossing. Separate visible digits/record time encoding from time advancement; do not call the units milliseconds.
candidates.removed_machinery: Three-byte packed timer state and decimal carry chain in regular gameplay.
candidates.remaining_boundaries: HUD tile conversion, original two-byte record format and legacy snapshot/debug encoding.
candidates.benefit: Time progression, record comparison and rendering have explicit independent roles, with a native quantity usable by future timing consumers.
candidates.difficulty_reason: Small state owner but saturation overshoot and accepted legacy byte states require care.
candidates.impact_reason: Removes arithmetic encoding across HUD and results, with a smaller reach than nitro.
candidates.risk: medium: saturation retains fraction, prepared/winner frames still advance, record precision truncates.
candidates.owners_order: RaceState owns timer. Prepared/running/finished service and postrace HUD paths advance at existing call positions; results read high/middle precision only.
preserve: increment sixteen source units, not wall time
prepared and winner frame service order
compatible public observations and restored historical saves
coverage_gaps: Fresh integrated timer/record boundary observations against source and faithful reference required.
Inventory accepted noncanonical BCD timer snapshot states; derive compatibility rather than reduce accepted state silently.
candidates.overlaps: M1 shares HUD/snapshot boundaries only; independent implementation.
candidates.bounded_scope: Timer and direct display/record consumers only; no scheduler cadence change.

candidates.title: Extract name/shop scene scheduling
candidates.current_design: The large scheduler mixes NMI service, frontend domain calls, window ownership transfer, retained history and scene dispatch. Names and Shop arms each contain domain advance plus fade/window/ack/completion handling.
candidates.proposed_model: Keep the NMI loop and dispatch order in place; move names and shop scene steps into cohesive methods returning an explicit yield/continue result. Retain distinct phase semantics rather than merge superficially similar branches.
candidates.before_after: Before: long Names/Shop match arms inside the scene pump. After: short dispatch arms calling advance_names_scene/advance_shop_scene with explicit scheduling result; each helper owns its complete scene handoff.
candidates.smell: Mixed responsibilities in a roughly 600-line scene pump obscure whether a frontend completion yields or advances again during the same NMI.
candidates.benefit: Future name/shop phase changes can be reviewed in one local method without navigating unrelated race/loss/NMI logic; explicit scheduling result makes same-NMI continuation reviewable.
candidates.difficulty_reason: Structural extraction with existing owners and explicit return values; no game model conversion.
candidates.impact_reason: Makes a central frontend orchestration boundary easier to maintain, bounded to two arms.
candidates.risk: medium: moving break/continue incorrectly changes visible waits or sound ordering.
candidates.owners_order: Keep Port/State ownership, shared window moves, pause history transfer, sound flush position, scene loop bounds and begin_shop/postrace sequence.
preserve: Names FinalWait starts contraction; Shop FinalWait starts expansion
Ack window reclaim and finish_page order
same-NMI Shop completion continuation versus Names yield
tests: port/src/game/tests.rs: existing natural frontend/race replay and snapshot contracts
coverage_gaps: Add targeted Game transition regressions for Ack/completion yield behavior before extraction; fresh natural frontend replay and relevant captures required.
candidates.overlaps: M1 changes domain shop stock; this changes only its scheduler caller. Neither requires the other.
candidates.bounded_scope: No new framework, new state owner or alteration to game model; only two frontend scene handlers.

investigation.strongest_conversion_considered: Native wallet balances replacing six digit arrays throughout awards, purchases and results.
investigation.why_deferred: Source shop normalization is deferred; raw byte wrap/sign threshold 8A, capped inactive conversion leaves unnormalized debit, and highest borrow mutates previous wallet tail or selected_wallet. A plain integer balance loses these conditional effects. Need a source-backed model of pending raw operations and accepted snapshots before offering this deeper conversion. See shop.trace.md and tests at lines 181-297.
investigation.next_probe: Characterize exact raw-wallet states at every normalization caller and reference natural capped-conversion entry; determine whether a native pending-debit model can preserve conditional alias effects without retaining digit machinery.
investigation.other_direction: Window/sprite continuation ownership already uses semantic enums and preserves observable NMI waits; removing them wholesale would not be a demonstrated modernization.
investigation.validation: 627 library tests pass; full optimized check and audit pass; prior bounded QA retained, no new gameplay certification.
